This game looks nice, and I tend to love TD games, however, I can't recommend this game because the Ai is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I was playing a skirmish map, and one of the graphite armoured kitties (the ones that need to be hit with upgraded lasers) got past my laser defenses, (2 twin shredders up front, 2 beam lasers in the middle, 1 heavy turret on the back left, 2 shredders/1 regular gatling turret on the back right) and out of nowhere, the next wave came rushing at me. I did not ONCE click on them to signal them to start the attack, they just did. So I have 4 turrets at the back hammering away on a cat they can't kill, and I have 2 lasers and 2 twin shredders which are overrun easily. I lose because my 4 turrets hammer away at the invincible kitty and weren't bothering to defend the base.

Another issue is what I mentioned before. The waves start without you, sometimes they don't and sometimes they do, it's a coin toss which you get, I've done everything, hell, I've refused eye contact with the bastards and they still come running.

Last issue is Skirmish mode, some levels are laughable broken. On the level I described with the 6 towers, I got $2500 to spend, on another level WITH THE SAME AMOUNT OF ENEMIES, I got $1250. The cheapest turrets cost $500, so you're stuck with 2, and if you place them in a bad position, that's it. Skirmish on that map is brutal. I have yet to get past wave 3. We need to be able to program the turrets to go after specific targets, and if that's already a thing, I haven't been properly tutorialized on it, and I've tried EVERYTHING.

When these issues are fixed and the game gets more balanced, then I'll recommend it, but as it is right now? It's just frustrating and not worth the money. If you do get the game, stick to the campaign, those levels are more fair and let's you ease into it. Skirmish throws everything at you at once with zero hesitation and it's not fun nor fair.

So, I never thought I'd be the tower defense type, but this game opened my eyes to it. It's a very well done game for vr and I never had much issues with it. Sadly I beat it quite quickly, once of normal and once on hard. I do wish it had a lot more levels because if you do manage to do them without fail, you will beat the game in your first day if you can stay on vr for extended periods of time. 
Still well worth getting it in my eyes however. It's story line isn't going to win a contest, but it's enough to keep the game moving. At that, immersion wise, it's not bad, but not great. You don't constantly think about how in this world you are a massive human who just makes towers. Or at least I didn't. The look of the game is very fitting in my eyes, and there are a good amount of alien cats to attack. It's without a doubt no shooter (though i do wish that was an aspect of it because that could add a bit more player immersion to the game.) but it is definitely a pretty good tower defense in my eyes. 

Should you buy it?
If you think it looks interesting from the video and pictures then yes with out a doubt I am willing to be you will enjoy it. Like I said I never thought I would like a tower defense and the vr aspect to it makes it pretty nice as well if you enjoy vr as much as I do. 
If you don't think you will enjoy it I would say you can give it a try, maybe find out like I did, because it is possible to return games as long as you are within the guide lines. 
If you without a doubt do not like tower defense but you think the vr aspect could change that, MAYBE try it. And if you don't like it return it. But it's up to you in the long run. 

Final notes:
It's not a long game, but there is progression so you aren't going to fly through it in an hour. You'll enjoy it on normal then maybe try hard, or just go right to hard. I think going into it on hard will make it more challenging then normal and in turn more enjoyable but it's up to you what you do with it once bought.

Very awesome game!  I am a big fan of Tower Defense games in general, and I really like ones like this which have you place towers strategically to win the war.

These levels are challenging, but not overwhelmingly, and you can keep learning by failing and readjust your strategy to overcome each level.  Due to my very impatient personality, I cannot afford to spend hours of my precious time trying to overcome a level.....it's just too frustrating for me.

I like the many towers available and their diffident capabilities.  This is a sign of a very creative developer.  The Tower upgrades are awesome as well.  All of this facilitates a game that calls for strategy to overcome.

By the time you get to the final level, you will be given sufficient resources to overcome the onslaught of kittens.  It took me a couple of tries on some of these levels, especially the last one, but it is not frustrating at all.  

I just cannot understand the very few negative reviews at the time of this writing. I did not experience anything that would cause me to write a negative review about this very creative and imaginative game by the Developer. 

It took me a little more than eight (8) hours to get through all fifteen (15) levels, and I know people that have paid much more than the full retail price of $15 for that much time to complete a game. There is good replay value as well after sufficient time has passed, and you forget how to overcome the level. So I will likely come back to this one after some time passes...it was that much fun that I want to play more than once.

I am surprised that this game was out since 2016, and I never noticed it until it went on sale.  Developer, if you are still out there, please keep your games coming. You are a very talented VR game creator.  Why have you not had any follow up games to this one?  It is obvious by the great reviews that this game is very popular in VR.

+ Many types and levels of towers - effective against many different types of kitties!
+ Nice graphic - it not might be obvious from flat screenshots, but this game is surprisingly beautiful
+ Free view - You can position camera to view over the battle or make yourself small and observe kitties from the ground (but you don't have to move while playing if it makes you motion sick).

- Stupid turrets - sometimes even when placed on perfect spot, turrets just shoot ground or target wrong kitties; it is shame you cannot hop into a turret yourself.
- Cannot set difficulty in skirmish (default one is insane) - 3 difficulty levels only in campaign mode; if you are in the middle of hard campaign and want relaxed gameplay or maybe show it to a beginner? well, the only option is to start again easy campaign and lost progress in hard one.
- Most time you need to look down which might hurt your neck after a long game session.
- Some achievements don't work - or there is no way to get some of them due to the difficulty

• Generally, this genre of games might not be much better in VR than on screen like other genres, at least with the current generation of headsets. In slow-paced games with a lot of waiting or just observing, you can feel the weight of your headset - but at least you have better view and control over the battlefield.

Kittypocalypse is a game about placing and upgrading the EXACT combination of towers in the EXACT right location at the EXACT right time. Do not be fooled by the cute kitties in the trailer. This game is freaking hard! Also, you'll be zoomed out most of the time trying to prevent the constant advance of their armored mechs, so usually you will just see them as cat-eared dots on a map :)

While this may sound like a less engaging experience than,s ay, Defense Grid or even Sanctum; I would stilll argue that it's compelling--albeit in a different way. Starting a level with 5 or 8 tower slots may feel too simple for a tower defense game, but it's still quite satisfying figuring out how to work with those tower slots to scale your defense. 

Wait too long to upgrade a tower, and some class of enemy will blow by you before it's too late. Upgrade a tower too soon, and you'll slaughter weaker enemies easily but not have the funds to upgrade the tower you *actuallly* need.

Definitely worth playing for tower defense fans, but I probably wouldn't start with Kittypocalypse if you're unfamiliar with the genre.
